grounding: sources/permit_limits.csv: LIMIT_FREQ_OF_ANALYSIS_CODE is populated on 105 limit rows with eight distinct opaque tokens (e.g. 05/WK, 01/07, 01/01, 09/99, 99/99) and no definition column or workspace legend for the field.

documents/farmington/final_permit.txt: NM0020583 Part I MEASUREMENT FREQUENCY uses human-readable text (Five/Week, Continuous, Daily, 2/month, Once/Quarter) that aligns with matched structured rows but never states or uses the opaque tokens.
documents/gcc/final_permit.txt: NM0000116 distinguishes 1/Day vs 1/Week in permit narrative for parameters whose structured rows carry 01/01 vs 01/07, without defining those tokens.
documents/aztec/final_permit.txt: NM0028762 states 1/Week, 2/Week, and 1/Day in plain text for rows carrying 01/07, 02/07, and 01/01 respectively, without defining the structured codes.
documents/farmington/final_permit.txt (lines 500–504, 518–520): WET retest reporting is conditional ('If required'), supporting that 09/99 rows are event-triggered rather than calendar-periodic.

documents/farmington/final_permit.txt (lines 63, 78): Flow is 'Continuous' with Totalizing Meter where structured rows carry 99/99, supporting that 99/99 denotes continuous monitoring rather than an ordinary sampling cadence.
interpretation: Workspace sources do not establish a general decoding of LIMIT_FREQ_OF_ANALYSIS_CODE into monitoring frequencies. Permit narrative text supplies human-readable frequencies for matched permit-parameter rows, but no workspace file authorizes those texts as a legend for the opaque tokens. Consistent CSV-to-permit alignment across three facilities is present in the packet but is explicitly non-dispositive. A supported negative finding applies only to 09/99 and 99/99: they do not establish ordinary calendar periodic sampling frequencies comparable to codes such as 01/07 or 05/WK—99/99 appears on continuous-flow parameters and 09/99 on conditional WET retest reporting.
remaining_uncertainty: Whether each calendar-structured token (05/WK, 01/01, 01/07, 02/07, 02/30, 01/90) encodes the human-readable MEASUREMENT FREQUENCY on its matched permit row; whether a reusable NN/XX or NN/WK encoding scheme exists beyond this workspace; how footnoted conditions (e.g. sampling on five different days, when discharging) modify nominal frequencies relative to the code field; whether DMR_FREQ_OF_ANALYSIS_CODE could disambiguate any limit-side codes.
